evidence: Hor. S. 1.9.1: ībam forte viā Sacrā
Cic. Planc. 65: Puteolōs forte vēnissem (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin says “I happened to …” with the verb and forte: forte vīdī, I happened to see. Sī forte, if by any chance; nisi forte, unless perhaps; forte fortūnā, by sheer luck (Ter. Eun. 134, Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Planc. 65: cum cāsū diēbus iīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Often beside forte; the opposite is cōnsiliō, on purpose.

phrases.latin: Ībam forte viā Sacrā, sīcut meus est mōs
phrases.english: I happened to be walking along the Sacred Way, as is my habit

phrases.latin: erat forte brūmae tempus et nivālis diēs
phrases.english: it happened to be midwinter, and a snowy day

phrases.latin: ut vēlōcissimus quoque, sī forte iter cum parvulō faciat, det manum et gradum suum minuat
phrases.english: as even the fastest walker, if he happens to be travelling with a little child, gives him his hand and shortens his step

forte.html: The ablative of the third-declension fors (de Vaan 236, s.v. fors: “abl. forte ‘by chance’”). Verg. A. 1.377, forte suā Libycīs tempestās adpulit ōrīs, and Hor. S. 1.9.1, ībam forte viā Sacrā: in both, forte su- and forte vi- are dactyls.
